toolProblems: computer left_click by ref or by coordinate is unreliable inside the canvas conversation rail: the rail auto-scrolls between the measurement and the click, so three presses landed on message DIVs instead of the intended button. A capture-phase pointerdown listener was needed to tell 'the click missed' from 'the button is dead'. Reliable recipe: scroll the element into view, verify document.elementFromPoint at the target, then click immediately — and re-verify afterwards.

computer left_click by coordinate refuses to run until a computer screenshot has been taken in that tab ('no screenshot dimensions cached'), including after navigations; the coordinate frame is 800×500 while the emulated CSS viewport is 1440×900 (factor 0.5556).

A JS video.play() in this headless pane is paused again immediately (a 'pause' event fires at currentTime 0), so playback can only be proven by clicking the native play control with a real mouse click.

get_page_text and read_page intermittently return an empty document for a freshly navigated tab while the page is in fact rendered (seen on both tabs); javascript_tool readouts and a screenshot disagreed with them for tens of seconds.
read_network_requests shows Next.js server actions only as 'POST <page url> → 200' with no body, so request payloads had to be captured with an inspection-only fetch wrapper.
arkcli 1.0.23 reports auth status logged_in=true while `usage stats` fails with an STS refresh error — 'logged in' is not the same as 'can query usage'.
findings: Canvas crash (new, no money impact, reproduced twice): approving a generation and then letting a second tab replay the same card, and separately confirming a 'Create variations' dialog, each threw the canvas into its error boundary — 'This canvas didn't open · It stopped loading part way through' — with console 'Minified React error #185' (maximum update depth exceeded). Both times the ledger was correct and a plain reload showed the true state, but the merchant sees a broken canvas immediately after paying.

'Try again' on a failed card gives no feedback at all (new): a trusted click reaches the button, the server action returns 200 and appends a fresh un-generated card, yet the conversation shows nothing, the button never enters its 'Queuing…' state and no error appears. Only a page reload reveals the new card. In this group that silence produced four identical clone cards from four presses. It is free today (coworkVaryCard is zero-spend by construction), but the same silence on a paid control would be a money bug.

The refusal copy on the retry is a genuine improvement worth keeping: approving the retried card was blocked before any provider call with 'One of your references is only 80×107 pixels — it needs to be at least 300 pixels on its shortest side. … nothing was sent. Reference 4QF05HQC', and Otto says the same thing in chat. That 80×107 px starting frame is the root cause of the 2026-09-11 provider 400 that produced the failed job in the first place — the failure class is now caught pre-charge.

Idempotency keys come in three families on this build, all consistent with the spec: 'cowork:<cardId>' for a confirmation card (the client sends the cardId, so a second tab replaying the same card cannot mint a second job), 'canvas:<sha256 of the material>' for a canvas Create variations, and 'asset:regen:<sha256>' for the Library panel's Regenerate. A 'Try again' clone gets a brand-new cardId, so its key is independent of the original by construction.

'Create variations' is not in the Library detail panel — it is only on the canvas node toolbar (Edit with Otto · Create variations · Animate · Download). The Library panel offers Regenerate · 1 credit, Animate · 11 credits, Crop and Generate edit · 1 credit instead. A merchant working from Library cannot reach the variations wording the spec row uses.

The variations dialog on this build makes exactly ONE image per confirmation ('Images 1 / Shape 1:1', no count picker), so 'variations' plural is never one settlement group of several pictures — each extra take is its own confirmation and its own settlement group.

The variation's Generation.entitySnapshot is empty ([]) while the source image's carries the product with its refHash. That is consistent with the path (the variation is an edit of the picture — 'What we sent to the engine' starts '<Image_1> is the image being edited.'), but it means lineage by element is lost one hop down: the variation is not linked to the product entity, only to the source generation.

Staging served 502s and a ChunkLoadError for roughly a minute mid-run (canvas blank, then fine on reload) while /api/health stayed ok with the same build sha c0d25917 — worth knowing before reading any single canvas failure as a product bug.
